title: Sophont’s Holon-S1 AI Maps Cancer Genes from Routine Slides to Avoid Costly Tests
summary:
A new AI platform can identify the underlying biology of a tumor without the need for traditional molecular diagnostics. Sophont's Holon-S1 tool analyzes digital images from biopsies or surgery to predict the activity and spatial location of genes and biological pathways. The model was validated using data from 15 different scanners across 16 organ types, utilizing both fresh-frozen and formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue to help bring personalized cancer care to more patients.

The platform outperformed two other models in a controlled comparison of spatial gene activity and has already flagged potential new biomarkers in colon and breast cancer. Sophont, which is backed by Delphi Ventures, is now seeking partnerships with research teams to integrate the technology into clinical workflows to help doctors choose treatments that better match individual tumors.

selectedTweets.text:
Cancer patients with the same diagnosis often have very different tumor biology.

Molecular testing can reveal underlying differences, but that's slow and expensive.

Introducing Holon-S1, our platform to predict genes and biomarkers from routine pathology slides.

• beats two other models at predicting spatial gene activity in a controlled comparison
• has identified potentially novel biomarkers in breast cancer and colon cancer
• evaluated across 16 organ types and more than 15 scanners, using slides from both formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded and fresh-frozen tissue.

We believe Holon-S1 has the potential to help researchers find new biomarkers in slides they already have, discover treatment targets, and bring more personalized cancer care within reach!

selectedTweets.text:
We've been training pathology and neuro foundation models at Sophont for a year now, and the pathology work is now good enough for real cancer research

Using routine tissue slides nearly all cancer patients already have, we predict spatially resolved genes and infer biological pathway activity

Hence, more cancer patients can have their tumors' biology molecularly interpreted to assess treatment options & discover biomarkers, which unfortunately isn't typically performed in routine standard of care

Looking forward to working with research teams to actually deploy the fruits of our research to cancer patients

selectedTweets.text:
A huge congratulations to @iScienceLuvr and @humanscotti of @SophontAI on the release of their new model, Holon-S1

This is a huge step in using AI to do targeted and personalized cancer treatment for each patient using tissue slides that are already collected in the process!

Let's walk through this new AI model 

- Start with a tissue slide from a biopsy or surgery, already collected as part of cancer diagnosis.

- Give Holon-S1 a digital image of that slide. It predicts which genes are active and where they’re active in the tissue.

- Researchers compare those predictions with how patients responded to treatment.

- Look for biological clues that could help predict treatment response or point to potential drug targets.

- Test the promising leads in the lab and through clinical studies.

- The longer term goal is to use validated findings to help doctors choose treatments that better match each patient’s tumor.

Take a few minutes and watch their video, its extremely compelling

If there's a way for you to work with the Sophont team, please reach out. The end goal of using AI to cure cancer is one of the highest order things we can do as a society
